= PGPonyCore source review and CyberChef recipe audit — 2026-11-05 =

== Reviewed source and scope ==

Read-only review of [`norsehorse-dev/PGPonyCore`](https://github.com/norsehorse-dev/PGPonyCore)
at commit [`86d23e0abc05a7135e46c6eab5aa215fea2025d6`](https://github.com/norsehorse-dev/PGPonyCore/tree/86d23e0abc05a7135e46c6eab5aa215fea2025d6).
The README identifies this snapshot as PGPony 8.4.0 and the project is licensed
Apache-2.0. The review covered the README, package manifest, security and
contribution notes, symmetric/OpenPGP code, the pairing module, and selected
tests/vectors. No upstream source was copied into this repository, and no Swift
build or test run was performed; Swift and Xcode are not installed in this
workspace.

== What the package is — and is not ==

- `Package.swift` declares an iOS-only Swift package with an iOS 17.6 deployment
  floor. The README notes that building its ML-DSA-65 path requires the iOS 26
  SDK/Xcode 26; that availability condition is separate from the package's
  deployment floor.
- The package depends on Apple frameworks (including CryptoKit, CommonCrypto,
  Security, and CoreNFC) and a pinned, vendored `liboqs.xcframework` for ML-KEM.
  The README says the symbols lifted into the core remain `internal` while its
  public API is still being defined. A Kotlin sibling is described as planned,
  not as an available package at this commit.
- It is therefore **not a drop-in Android or browser dependency**. Importing it
  into a standalone HTML5 app is not supported by this package. A browser app
  would need a separately implemented JavaScript/WebCrypto solution or another
  browser-compatible library, with its own tests and interoperability evidence.
- The OpenPGP core includes packet parsing/building, key and signature work,
  classical and post-quantum algorithms, smart-card code, PGP/MIME, and a
  passphrase-only symmetric path. `PGPonyPair` is a separate local-network
  pairing module and explicitly shares no code with the OpenPGP core.

== Symmetric OpenPGP mechanics observed in source ==

The symmetric writer emits a classic `gpg -c`-compatible message: a v4 SKESK
(packet tag 3) with iterated-and-salted S2K, SHA-256, an 8-byte salt and the
OpenPGP coded count; AES-256; and an SEIPD v1 packet (tag 18) using CFB plus the
Modification Detection Code (MDC). The generated salt is random. This describes
the writer's stated format, not a claim that a PGPony build was executed here.

The decrypt path contains readers for v4, v5, and v6 SKESK forms. The v4 reader
handles simple, salted, and iterated-salted S2K. The v5 reader includes classic
S2K and Argon2 S2K plus AEAD session-key protection. The v6 reader handles the
Argon2-based form. The packet parser also contains SEIPD v1/v2 and tag-20 AEAD
handling (including OCB). The cipher-ID helper in the reviewed symmetric path
accepts AES-128/192/256. These modern forms are broader than the current local
CyberChef symmetric-decrypt operation.

A targeted search of this checkout's upstream Swift test tree did not find a
direct test of the symmetric writer/decrypt entry point or a file named
`SymmetricAEADv5Tests`, despite a source comment referring to that test name.
The source comments claim GnuPG verification for parts of the v5 path, but that
claim was not independently rerun here. Do not treat it as a known-answer vector
for a new browser implementation.

== PGPonyPair is a protocol, not a generic cipher recipe ==

The separate `PGPonyPair` module implements an application-specific v1 pairing
protocol: X25519 key agreement, HMAC-SHA256 commitment, transcript hashing,
HKDF-SHA256 key derivation, a human-comparison six-digit code, and sequenced
AES-256-GCM messages with protocol-bound nonce/AAD. Its tests include shared,
deterministic JSON vectors and full in-memory session replays. It also has QR
invite and Network-framework TCP transport code. This can support an
educational, protocol-specific vector inspector if desired, but it is not an
OpenPGP message recipe, an IETF-standard generic encryption construction, or a
standalone cipher to add under an AES/HMAC title.

== Local CyberChef duplicate and coverage check ==

The local kitchen already defines `pgpArmorCheck` and `pgpSymDecrypt`, and its
recipe packs already include **OpenPGP Armor (Kleopatra / GnuPG)** and
**OpenPGP Symmetric Message (SKESK / SEIPD)**. No duplicate operation or recipe
pack was added.

`pgpSymDecrypt` currently handles v4 SKESK with no encrypted-session-key field,
AES-128/192/256, iterated-and-salted S2K type 3 with SHA-1 or SHA-256, and SEIPD
v1 CFB+MDC. It deliberately rejects encrypted-session-key SKESK, non-AES
ciphers, non-v4 SKESK, SEIPD v2, and tag-20 AEAD messages. Its existing tests
use GnuPG control messages for AES-128 and AES-256 and assert the decoded
plaintext and MDC; they also cover altered ciphertext, wrong passphrases, raw
packet input, and explicit refusal of out-of-scope PKESK/AEAD messages.

The static Crypto Cookbook had no dedicated OpenPGP entry. A **Reference** card
was added to document the existing classic recipe, its test evidence, PGPonyCore's
broader source-level formats, and the precise local coverage gap. This does not
claim that the modern PGPonyCore formats are implemented in CyberChef.

== Decision and implementation gate ==

- Keep the existing two OpenPGP recipe packs; do not add a duplicate.
- Do not port PGPonyCore's modern symmetric formats or PGPonyPair yet. A port
  needs independent vectors for each packet/profile, differential testing
  against an independent implementation, malformed/tampered cases, resource
  bounds for S2K/Argon2, and browser-specific security review.
- At the time of this source-review snapshot, the Android consolidation request
  and follow-up HTML5 alternative were not yet a defined application scope. The
  repository had 89 top-level directories under `public/apps`, but only one
  Android Gradle project was found in the searched inventory. The later round-62
  follow-up created a narrowly scoped, separate OpenPGP.js browser app (not a
  PGPonyCore port); see
  [`openpgp-workbench-v1-implementation-2026-11-05.md`](openpgp-workbench-v1-implementation-2026-11-05.md).
  Android consolidation remains next, pending its target set and acceptance
  criteria.

- Local kitchen: [`public/apps/cyberchef/index.html`](../public/apps/cyberchef/index.html).
- Local independent control tests: [`tests/openpgp-sym-decrypt.test.mjs`](../tests/openpgp-sym-decrypt.test.mjs) and [`tests/openpgp-armor.test.mjs`](../tests/openpgp-armor.test.mjs).
- Public OpenPGP specifications: [RFC 4880](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4880) and [RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580). LibrePGP v5 details in PGPonyCore remain implementation-specific where they are not covered by those RFCs.
